claims.summary: For alpha_1,alpha_2 in (0,infinity] (no curve condition), every L>0, X,Y independent uniform samples of size N in [0,1]^2 and levels t_1,t_2 in [1,log N] with t_1^(1/alpha_1)/t_2^(1/alpha_2) -> infinity and e^(2 t_2) <= (L^2/8) log N t_1^(1/alpha_1) t_2^(1/alpha_2), with probability tending to one some matching has |X_i^1-Y^1_pi(i)| <= L sqrt(log N/N) t_1^(1/alpha_1) for every i and at most 2N e^(-t_2) pairs with |X_i^2-Y^2_pi(i)| > L sqrt(log N/N) t_2^(1/alpha_2). At (4,4) with t_1=log N it covers t_2 <= (5/8) log log N + (1/8) log t_2 + O(1).
claims.assessment: Working proof: cells of width about D/8 and height about H (the two levels' boxes), any matching inside cells, leftovers matched by column order one-dimensionally; the strip discrepancy is O(omega sqrt N) by Doob's inequality for the martingale U(x)/(1-x), and every three-column window holds about sqrt N (D/H)^(1/2) leftovers of each sample (Poissonization, lower tail for nonnegative sums); the leftovers number about N/sqrt k, within 2N e^(-t_2) by the hypothesis on t_2.
claims.rationale: Proves mixed level consequences of the condition with the first level up to the maximum and the second low, beyond the elementary cells baseline; mixed levels with bounded box ratio or a high second level, and the coupling of levels, remain.
claims.next_action: Mixed levels with bounded box ratio or e^(2 t_2) beyond log N t_1^(1/alpha_1) t_2^(1/alpha_2), e.g. (4,4), t_1=log N, t_2=sqrt(log N).

relationships: The equal-level case; together they cover a pair of levels when equal, or when the second level is low and the first box larger by a factor tending to infinity.
The top level in both coordinates; here the first coordinate's top level holds with the second coordinate low.
Same setting; that corollary reduces the whole condition to a discrepancy bound, this proves two levels of the condition directly.
The counts it supplies are those the condition implies, at two levels.
Mixed level consequences hold when the second level is low relative to log N times the two boxes and the first box is larger by a factor tending to infinity.
